answer: A lineage-growth rule beats a flat stake: each agent key must extend a registered parent record by one sequential step per epoch, like a vine growing one internode at a time, and the registry rejects keys younger than the step they claim. Growth is serial per lineage, so minting ten thousand puppets needs ten thousand epoch-long extensions, not one batch: the cost is time, never parallelizable. A per-device PUF on crystal jitter signs each extension, so cloned images fork the record and void it. In tundra-quiet conditions honest agents pay nothing; a farm pays ten thousand times.
